clue.text: Soldier with brother, a comedian

blocks.note: a Tommy is a British private soldier
'Oh brother!' and 'coo!' are both exclamations of surprise
a as in 'five pounds a head', meaning per

explanation.surface: A soldier and his brother, one of whom is a funny man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brother' looks like a sibling, but it is the exclamation, as in 'Oh brother!'; coo is the British equivalent. The comedian himself served as a trooper in the Royal Horse Guards.
explanation.definitionFit: Tommy Cooper was a much-loved British television entertainer famous for his fez and deliberately bungled magic tricks.

clue.text: Article’s penned on what sounds like problem group

indicators.note: something penned is shut inside an enclosure, so one piece sits within another
this phrase asks for a word that is said the same as another but spelt differently

blocks.note: the definite article
re means on or concerning
a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: A newspaper article written about a troublesome group of people.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Article' stands for 'has', so the article has the next piece penned inside it. 'Problem' is a schoolroom sum, not a difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: A threesome is a set of three people or things, so it is a small group.

clue.text: Support for fencing sheep that’s a life-saver

indicators.note: a fence goes round a field, so the first piece encloses the second

blocks.note: a mast is a supporting pole
a ewe is a female sheep

explanation.surface: A post holding up a sheep fence that turns out to save a life.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a description, not a synonym: an RAF airman's inflatable life jacket was nicknamed after the buxom actress.
explanation.definitionFit: A mae west is wartime slang for an inflatable life jacket, an item that keeps a person afloat and alive.

clue.text: Standard flying, introduction to Tricky Dicky’s enthralling a Republican

indicators.note: things sent flying are scattered every which way, so the letters land in a new order
an introduction comes at the start, so only the opening letter is wanted
to enthral is to hold captive, so one group of letters holds the other

blocks.note: first letter of the word
taken as written, apostrophe dropped
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A flag flies as Nixon, 'Tricky Dicky', wins over a fellow Republican.
explanation.walkthrough: Tricky Dicky was the nickname of US President Richard Nixon, a Republican, which makes the surface hang together; here the words simply supply letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardstick is a measure against which other things are judged, which is exactly what a standard is.

clue.text: Papa’s next to this exceptionally large coach

blocks.note: OS is the abbreviation for outsize
a railway coach is a car

explanation.surface: Dad stands beside a huge bus.
explanation.walkthrough: Papa looks like a father, but it is the NATO alphabet word for P; the word for O sits immediately before it.
explanation.definitionFit: In the radio spelling alphabet the codeword for O comes right before Papa, so Papa is its neighbour.

clue.text: Student, seized by local roughly, is put out

indicators.note: what is seized is gripped and held, so this piece sits inside the others

blocks.note: a local is one's neighbourhood pub
L for learner, a student
-ish means approximately

explanation.surface: A student grabbed roughly by a local resident ends up annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' is not a resident but British slang for one's regular pub; 'put out' reads as annoyed, but means issued.
explanation.definitionFit: To put out a book or statement is to issue it to the public, the plain sense of publishing.

clue.text: Programme is lacking in direction

indicators.note: lacking something means being without it, so some letters are taken away

blocks.note: a routine is a regular programme of activity
taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: A television programme criticised for being aimless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a preposition joining the clue, but it is the very pair of letters to be dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A route is the way taken to a destination, so it is a direction one follows.

clue.text: Somewhat dulcet or mellifluous singer?

indicators.note: somewhat means only to some extent, so just part of the following words is used

blocks.note: runs across the end of the first word, the whole middle word and the start of the last

explanation.surface: Is this sweet-voiced, honeyed performer a singer?
explanation.walkthrough: Mel Tormé, the American crooner nicknamed 'the Velvet Fog', is lurking in plain sight in the descriptive words.
explanation.definitionFit: Mel Tormé was an American jazz vocalist and songwriter, so he is an example of a singer.

clue.text: Rouse a slip when openers swap? It’s what bowler should do

indicators.note: openers here are the opening sounds of words, and trading them is the Reverend Spooner's famous verbal blunder

blocks.note: rouse means wake, and a slip of paper is a ticket

explanation.surface: A cricket picture: wake up the fielder at slip so the bowler can get a batsman out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slip' looks like the cricket fielding position, which suits the surface, but it is a paper ticket. In cricket a bowler's aim is to dismiss batsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, a bowler dismissing a batsman is said to have got a wicket, which is the bowler's chief job.

clue.text: Stagger and jump, hemmed in by cliffs

blocks.note: to rock is to sway or stagger
a bound is a leap

explanation.surface: Someone lurching and leaping while trapped between cliff faces.
explanation.walkthrough: The two verbs sound like a climber in trouble, but each simply supplies one half of the compound adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock-bound describes a coast or place surrounded and enclosed by rocky crags.

clue.text: Lovely rings for 19 staff

blocks.note: a dish is an attractive person
washers are flat metal or rubber rings

explanation.surface: A beauty wearing rings on behalf of the staff.
explanation.walkthrough: The 19 refers to the answer at 19-across, KITCHEN, so the definition means kitchen staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who scrub pots and plates in a restaurant are among the lowliest employees in its cooking area.

clue.text: Banks perhaps getting tip from security guards

indicators.note: a tip is an end point, so a single extreme letter is wanted

blocks.note: Gordon Banks was England's goalkeeper in the 1966 World Cup win
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Banks taking advice from their security staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banks' looks like financial institutions, but it is the famous English football goalkeeper; 'guards' looks like a verb, but is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Keepers are custodians who look after and protect something, the same as guards or wardens.

clue.text: They may sack bishop protecting assistant close to satanists

indicators.note: to protect is to shield by surrounding, so one piece wraps another
the close of a word is its end, so its final letter is wanted

blocks.note: RR stands for Right Reverend, a bishop's title
an aide is an assistant
last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Churchgoers might dismiss a bishop who shields a helper who is near to devil-worshippers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack' reads as fire from a job, but means plunder, as invaders do to a town.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiders are attackers who storm a place and loot it, which is what sacking a town means.

clue.text: Many drinking loudly, being high

indicators.note: a drinker takes something in, so one piece is swallowed by another

blocks.note: a lot means many
f, forte, is the musical mark for loud

explanation.surface: Lots of people drinking noisily and getting high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being high' suggests intoxication, which suits the drinkers, but it means simply up in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloft means up overhead or in the air, so something aloft is situated at height.

clue.text: Food prepared it’s wiser to keep hot?

indicators.note: food that is prepared has been worked up from raw ingredients, so the letters get made into something new
to keep something is to hold on to it, so one letter is held within the rest

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Kitchen advice: cooked food is better kept warm.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole sentence reads like sensible cooking advice; 'prepared' is the signal to rework the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish stew is a traditional dish of mutton or lamb with potatoes and onions, an example of a meal.

clue.text: Cut in top leaves colourist with overlay half-finished

indicators.note: when the top goes away the word loses its head, so its opening letter is dropped
a job half finished stops midway, so only part of the word is used

blocks.note: a tinter is someone who adds colour
a veneer is a thin overlaid surface layer

explanation.surface: A painter departs when the overlay is left half done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like foliage on top of a tree, but is the verb 'goes away'. 'Cut in' reads as a haircut, but means to interrupt.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut in on a conversation or dispute is to interrupt or step into it, the sense of intervening.

clue.text: Quality of port selection from delicatessen in Watford on the up

indicators.note: a selection is a portion picked out, so a run of letters is taken from the words
in a down clue going up means reading from bottom to top, back to front

blocks.note: the run of letters from the end of the first word through to the start of the last

explanation.surface: A deli in Watford is selling port that is improving.
explanation.walkthrough: Tawny port is aged in wood barrels until it turns a brownish-gold colour; Watford is a town just north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Tawny port is the classic wood-aged style, so its characteristic brownish colour is a quality of the drink.

clue.text: Resist texts now and then, faced with froideur – this may come from waiter

indicators.note: something done now and then happens at intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: froideur is coldness of manner, which is icy
to buck is to resist or oppose, as in buck the trend
the second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: Someone trying not to message, while facing a chilly reception from a waiter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faced with' means the cold piece is placed in front of the rest. The waiter is the one bringing a chilled bottle to the table.
explanation.definitionFit: A waiter brings wine or champagne to the table chilled in a container full of frozen cubes.

clue.text: Put off hack?

blocks.note: surface reading: to discourage a jobbing journalist
setter's reading: a hack is also a riding mount, and putting a rider off one means throwing them from the saddle

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' wants to be a hack writer, but it is a horse for ordinary riding; 'put off' means removed from it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be thrown or knocked from one's mount, as in a joust, is the literal meaning of the verb.

clue.text: Perhaps French and Saunders finally begins to appear

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the closing letter is wanted

blocks.note: Dawn French is a British comic actress, an example of a Dawn
last letter of the name

explanation.surface: French and Saunders, the British comedy double act, at last start to turn up.
explanation.walkthrough: French and Saunders reads as the comedy duo of Dawn French and Jennifer Saunders, but the two names are split and used separately.
explanation.definitionFit: When something dawns it starts to become visible or evident, like daylight at sunrise.

clue.text: Imposing old lady starts to dust office with Pledge

indicators.note: starts are beginnings, so only the opening letters are taken

blocks.note: first letters of the two words
a wager is a stake or pledge

explanation.surface: A grand old woman begins cleaning an office with Pledge furniture polish.
explanation.walkthrough: Pledge is a well-known brand of furniture polish, which makes the dusting picture work; here it means a stake.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowager is a dignified elderly woman, typically a titled widow, so she is a stately old lady.

clue.text: Part of house where gong is sounded?

blocks.note: first meaning: the room where food is cooked
second meaning: musicians' slang for an orchestra's percussion section

explanation.walkthrough: The dinner gong suggests the dining room or hall, but in orchestral slang the percussion section, gongs included, is called the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: The room for cooking is one part of a home, and orchestral slang applies the same word to the drums and cymbals section.

clue.text: Reports regularly neglected trawl-nets

indicators.note: ignoring at even intervals means every second letter goes, leaving the others

blocks.note: first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters

explanation.surface: Fishing reports say the trawl-nets keep being left unattended.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen is ignored: the two words are read as one run of nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tales are stories or accounts people pass on, so they can be reports of events.

clue.text: New single, initially tuneful composition

indicators.note: initially means at the beginning, so the word's opening letter is wanted

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
one means single
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A new single record that is, from the start, a melodious piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Single' looks like a pop record but is just the number; 'composition' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a piece of music written for nine players or voices, so it is a type of musical work.

clue.text: Something Texan needs to crack when driving?

definitions.text: Something Texan needs to crack when driving?

blocks.clueFragment: Something Texan needs to crack when driving?
blocks.note: surface reading: a Texas motorist who must break something or solve a problem on the road

blocks.clueFragment: Something Texan needs to crack when driving?
blocks.note: setter's reading: a cowboy driving cattle cracks a whip made of untanned leather

explanation.walkthrough: 'Driving' suggests a car, but it is herding cattle on a trail drive; 'crack' is the snap of a whip.
explanation.definitionFit: Untanned cattle skin is braided into whips, and cowboys crack such whips to drive their herds.

clue.text: Understanding music genre receives approving remark

indicators.note: to receive is to take in, so one piece is taken inside another

blocks.note: trance is a style of electronic dance music
olé is a shout of approval, as at a bullfight

explanation.surface: A style of music gets a word of praise and wins people over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Understanding' sits at the front looking like an adjective describing the genre, but it is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerance is patient acceptance of others' views or behaviour, a form of sympathetic understanding.

clue.text: Old people scratch in the ears

indicators.note: what reaches the ears is heard, so the word is judged by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: a graze is a scrape or scratch on the skin

explanation.surface: Elderly folk scratching inside their ears.
explanation.walkthrough: Older people are informally called greys after their hair colour, as in 'the grey vote'.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey hair marks age, so the elderly are informally referred to collectively by that colour.

clue.text: An item has tweeters raging

definitions.note: a singular phrase for a couple, defining a plural noun

indicators.note: something raging is out of control and wild, so the letters are thrown about

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gossip story about a social-media couple whose followers are furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Item' looks like a thing or a news story, but it is the informal word for a romantic couple.
explanation.definitionFit: When two people are an item they are in a romantic relationship, a pair of lovers.
